findings.case: In M1 the principal runs `git init` for a new project. An agent's run creates a room and links `main` while the repository has a provisional identity P and the branch has no remote. The run then makes the first commit, so the clone has a root commit R, and later runs `git push -u origin main`. Each time, the identity the hook handlers compute for the branch changes: (P, no remote, main), then (R, no remote, main), then (R, origin URL, main). A changed remote URL, such as https to ssh, gives the same kind of change.
findings.problem: No requirement says whether the room's branch link, which names the provisional identity, then names the bound or pushed branch. One implementer maps it automatically. Another treats the change as LANE-02's identity change that needs a widening rebind, so until the principal acts the branch belongs to no room and the run's later events route to its personal room, a move LANE-01 does not allow. No requirement says the bind or rebind is recorded as an event either, and room state needs that event to derive from the record alone (I10).
findings.fix: Binding a provisional repository identity, and rebinding a provisional branch identity when the branch first has an upstream at a hook event, MUST each be recorded as a structural event in the recording device seat's personal-room writer. The event names the provisional and the new identity, and a tombstone keeps it. Every branch link naming the provisional identity MUST then name the new one, with no principal act and no move of the branch; a tie with another link resolves under LANE-31, and the change is audited and shown. Only a change to an identity already bound needs LANE-02's widening rebind.

findings.case: On a macOS node the login keychain is locked, because the principal works over SSH or the machine slept; on a Linux node the keyring is not yet unlocked. The device key and the seat keys the core keeps are still in the platform key store, but the core cannot read them when a hook handler or MCP server starts. A new run's personal-room seat needs a seat certificate from the device key (PRV-11).
findings.problem: The SRS says what happens when a key is missing (mint a new one, with a new seat and writer under SEC-27) and when the node identity changes or is unavailable (the whole earlier record counts as received). It says nothing about a store that holds the key but refuses access. Three implementers can differ. One mints a new device key and seat keys: every device seat restarts with no add or role, and two device keys exist once the store unlocks. Another reads node identity from the store, counts a changed identity, and makes the whole record received, so the principal's pins stop restoring. A third appends nothing and waits. The key set, room state, membership, trust levels and active pins all differ.
findings.fix: A platform key store that holds a key but refuses access (locked or denied) MUST count neither as a missing key (SEC-10) nor as an unavailable node identity (REC-24). The core MUST mint no key and append nothing that needs the refused key; the hook handlers leave ingest markers as REC-19 says for a run whose MCP server does not yet hold its run-seat key. The core MUST audit and count the refusal, show it in `parinn status`, and resume once the store grants access.

findings.case: In M5 a long-running run R recalls a `web` event X that carries an injection. SEC-13 taints R, so the example PreToolUse hook handler asks for approval of sensitive action classes. After the purge, nothing in the record says the returned item was untrusted. An implementer that derives taint from the record clears R's taint, which removes SEC-13's approval step from a run that saw the injection. An implementer that keeps the taint set from before the purge gets a rebuild that differs (ADM-08, I10). The grid's Purge row names ADM-07 for trust levels, and ADM-07 does not decide this.

findings.case: In M1 run R calls `event_expand` and receives a `web` event X that carries an injection. The harness records the enveloped result as R's tool result T, which ParleyInn ingests and indexes. The principal then quarantines X. After a compaction, R calls `event_search` in its default `run` scope. The search matches T, and `event_expand` on T returns X's text again, enveloped.
findings.problem: SEC-12 withholds what its selector covers, and SEC-31 extends a purge to copies of the content in recorded recall results, but no requirement says whether a quarantine reaches those copies; 'as a purge keeps what it removes' can be read either way. One implementer withholds X's item inside T and another returns it. Under the second, the quarantine fails for the very run that recalled the content, against M1's exit criterion 'quarantine effective' and I5.
findings.fix: A quarantine MUST also withhold, on every path it covers, each copy of covered content that SEC-31 would erase in a purge, such as the item naming a covered address in a recorded recall result, and return a quarantine marker in its place. Its release MUST make those copies available again.

findings.case: In M3 a run's `SessionEnd` hook handler hits an internal error, such as a full disk or a corrupt page, before it writes its ingest marker, and fails open as §9.1 says ('Exit 0, audit'). The same happens when the harness is killed and no `SessionEnd` fires. The transcript lines are ingested later from the ingest position, but the end observation existed only in the hook's input and is lost.
findings.problem: Only a hook handler cut short by its budget leaves an ingest marker. One that fails open keeps nothing of its hook's input, and no requirement says when a run with no recorded end closes its last span. One implementer leaves that span open for ever, so LMK-02 never makes its landmark and the landmark index never covers the run's last work. Another closes it at some later point. Spans and landmarks differ between the two, though each is deterministic.
findings.fix: A hook handler that fails open MUST, where it still can, leave an ingest marker holding the events its hook's input makes (REC-13). LMK-01 MUST close the last span of a run with no recorded end at a point the record fixes, such as the start of a later run in the same harness session. Where no such point exists, the open span MUST get a landmark marked open, whose address range grows as events arrive.

findings.case: In M3 encryption at rest is off, the default until SEC-09 ships in M5. The principal purges a range of a run. Then a harness resume or rewind rewrites that run's transcript (ASM-04), which still holds the purged lines, now at new positions. As REC-07 says, the hook handlers leave the new generation to `parinn ingest`.
findings.problem: The purged lines' content is erased, so no prefix comparison can match them, and the earlier generation's positions do not locate them in the new one. Nothing says what `parinn ingest` does next. One implementer ingests the new generation past the equal prefix, bringing the purged content back into the store and the index as `ingested` and undoing a purge that SEC-31 says ingest must refuse. Another refuses the whole generation and loses the run's new lines (I1).
findings.fix: With no at-rest key, `parinn ingest` MUST ingest a new generation of a source with a purged range only after it shows the principal, by position and count, the lines past the equal prefix and takes the principal's confirmation at a terminal of which lines to ingest. Each line left out MUST be refused, audited and counted.

themes.title: Binding a provisional repository or branch identity: which links follow it, and which event records it
themes.reason: The finding is partly refuted. LANE-02 already says a repository identity is 'bound once, at the first hook event, by a replicating structural event'. Both rows also say the provisional identity is bound later 'without rewriting the record', which points to links naming the provisional identity staying valid. That leaves no contradiction: LANE-02's widening-only rebind governs a change in the repository identity a directory resolves to, LANE-01's 'rebound on push' governs a branch's provisional identity, and both statements can hold together. Two things stay open. No row says whether the move from provisional to bound counts as LANE-02's 'change' that needs a widening rebind. No row says that the bind event, or any event for the branch rebind on push, names the provisional identity, which room state needs in order to derive from the record alone (I10). Neither gap forces an invariant break if built as written, because an implementer can record the event. LANE-01 and LANE-02 are M1, so this is in scope. The lifecycle grid (§8.5) has no row for either bind.

themes.reason: No text settles this case. SEC-10 covers a key 'missing from where it is kept', and REC-24 covers an 'unavailable' node identity value. Neither names a locked or denied store that still holds the key. NFR-06 only makes a hook handler fail open and audit, and does not say whether the core mints keys, certifies seats (PRV-11) or appends. No invariant is broken as written. Minting anew keeps every event (I1), and derived state stays a function of the logs and the key set (I10). The SRS does not say where node identity comes from, so the REC-24 consequence follows only from an implementer's choice. SEC-10, REC-24 and PRV-11 are all M1, and a locked keychain or keyring is an ordinary M1 condition, so the gap is real and in scope. No open question covers it.

themes.reason: Confirmed against the text. RCL-07 records only the addresses of the returned events. ADM-07's tombstone keeps provenance only 'of each purged act, tombstone and event the key set holds', and OQ-44 confirms that reading, so a purged `web` tool result keeps none. SEC-31 also erases the envelope copy, with its `trust` field, from the recorded tool result. After a purge nothing in the record says the returned item was untrusted, and ADM-07's 'derive as before but for the purged content' does not decide whether taint stays. This is not an invariant break. Clearing the taint opens no new path into the model, so I2 holds. Both readings are deterministic, so I10 holds as long as the implementer derives taint from the record. SEC-13 and REC-15 are M5 and ADM-07 is M3, so this is in scope.

themes.reason: SEC-12 withholds 'what it covers', meaning what its selector matches. A quarantine of X by address does not match the tool-result event T that holds X's text inside a recorded envelope. 'As a purge (ADM-07) keeps what it removes' can be read as reaching the copies that ADM-07 and SEC-31 erase, or as only describing how covered events are withheld. What comes back through T is enveloped and pulled by an explicit recall, so I2 holds. themes.title: The last span of a run whose end was never recorded
themes.reason: Confirmed. LMK-01 closes a run's last span only at an end that the hook handlers record from `SubagentStop` or `SessionEnd`. Under NFR-06 a handler that fails open only audits, and NFR-02 and REC-13 require an ingest marker only for work cut short by the budget. A killed harness fires no `SessionEnd`. As written, the span stays open, and since LMK-02 makes landmarks only for closed spans, the run's last work never gets a landmark. No invariant breaks. The events stay recallable by address (I1), and 'open for ever' is a deterministic function of the record (I10). The alternative, closing the span at some later point, would go beyond what LMK-01 allows rather than follow it. LMK P0 is M3, and REC-13 is M3 and M5, so this is in scope. The grid's 'Run end' row assumes the end was recorded.

themes.title: What `parinn ingest` does with a new transcript generation of a purged source when there is no at-rest key
themes.reason: Confirmed. With no at-rest key, REC-07 defers the new generation to `parinn ingest` but says nothing about what that command does differently. Its general rule, ingest past the longest content-equal prefix, would re-ingest the purged lines. Their content and commitment key are erased (ADM-07), there is no keyed hash (SEC-08 needs the at-rest key), and SEC-31's recorded positions are positions in the earlier generation. This is not blocking. SEC-31's 'refuse ... to ingest them again' can be read narrowly as those recorded positions, which leaves REC-07 and SEC-31 both satisfiable, and re-ingesting breaks no invariant: I1 permits a purge but does not require that content to stay gone, and ingested events are untrusted under REC-22, so I2 holds. It still defeats the principal's purge. It occurs in M3 to M5, because SEC-09 at-rest encryption is a P1 SHOULD that arrives in M5 and is never the default.

findings.case: Requested check. Through M1 to M5 the rule holds without being written down: LMK-06 does not ship, and LMK-02 keeps every landmark, and so the landmark index INJ-01 puts in the restore block, structural only. Once LMK-06 ships, one implementer reads 'trusted fields' as the span's sanitized structural fields, which count as trusted whatever the event's trust level. That implementer renders a headline such as 'Edited fts.rs six times; 2 Bash errors' from a fixed template. That text is fixed text ParleyInn ships plus sanitized structural fields, so INJ-03 lets the restore builder take it as TrustedText, I2 admits it, and nothing in INJ-01, INJ-02 or INJ-07 keeps it off each landmark line of the restore block. A second implementer reads 'trusted fields' as trusted event text, such as a `user` line typed in interactive mode, and keeps headlines out of the block under INJ-03.
findings.problem: No requirement states the model's rule that a natural-language headline is no structural field and never reaches a restore block. findings.case: From M1, one MCP server serves a harness session's main run and its subagents' runs. A subagent calls `event_search` with the default scope, and the MCP call carries nothing that names the subagent. Several rules need to know the calling run: RCL-05 for the `run` scope, RCL-07 for the writer the recall event goes to, CMP-02 (M4) for whose kernel namespace `kernel_exec` uses, and SEC-13 (M5) for which run carries the recall taint. Implementers would split three ways. One credits every call to the main run, so the subagent searches the parent's history as its own `run` scope and the parent takes the subagent's taint. Another refuses the call. A third matches it afterwards against the tool_use line in the transcript.

Where it cannot tell, the `run` scope MUST cover only the runs the call may belong to and be logged as extending recall, the recall event MUST name each of those runs, SEC-13 MUST taint each, and a room act MUST be refused, audited and counted.

SEC-10's opt-in to taking keys from the environment, raising `pin_budget.max_model_tokens` or `recall.max_k`, and turning on `restore_block.on_prompt` or `restore_block.landmarks_on_start` fall under neither clause. Even SEC-10's 'under ADM-04' points to a rule that does not list that opt-in. It is not blocking. Whatever a restore block carries stays `TrustedText`, and recall stays pull-only and enveloped. An agent of the same OS user editing config.toml falls under the residual risks. I can quote no invariant clause that these changes break as built.

quotes.text: until then each setting it changes MUST stand as it stood, while any other change that only tightens, such as turning a B1–B3 component off, needs no acceptance
never inherited from the environment unless a configuration setting under ADM-04 opts in

themes.gap: M1 must decide whether each change ADM-04 does not list and that does not only tighten waits for the widening acceptance. Examples are SEC-10's opt-in to keys from the environment, raising `pin_budget.max_model_tokens` or `recall.max_k`, and turning on `restore_block.on_prompt` or `restore_block.landmarks_on_start` (ADM-04, SEC-10, INJ-02, INJ-04, PIN-08).

themes.title: Membership and role of a run seat a new key starts in the personal room
themes.reason: Settled. SEC-27's 'inherits no … role' only stops role assignments carrying over. LANE-16's default rule, whose M1 part covers it, still gives 'a run's personal-room seat' the contributor role, and the new seat is one. LANE-25 makes 'a run's personal-room seat' a member with no add. That wording is generic, so it covers every personal-room seat of the run, and the REC-24 scenario reads it the same way. In M1–M5, LANE-01 never refuses an event routed to a personal-room seat. LANE-23's M2 join request comes from 'the run seat its MCP server then holds', which is the new seat. Checking room acts against membership (LANE-24, LANE-25) and naming the seat id in the restore block (LANE-30) ship in M7, where LANE-25's wording already covers this seat.

quotes.text: but a run's personal-room seat and its seat in a room it created MUST have the contributor role
a run's personal-room seat is a member from the run's first event
inherits no add, role or appointment, and is a member only as LANE-23 and LANE-25 say

themes.title: `parinn uninstall` after a SEC-22 refusal: ADM-02's 'Otherwise' branch requires removing hooks with no act recorded
themes.reason: The finding holds up as a contradiction in M3–M5 behaviour (ADM-02 changed in M3, SEC-22 in M1). Managed policy requires an authenticator, and presence proofs do not exist yet, so SEC-22 refuses the widening act turning capture off. OWN-22 did not refuse it, so ADM-02's 'Otherwise' branch applies, and it requires reversing exactly the harness configuration changes `install` made, the hook registrations included. ADM-02's first clause allows removing the hook registrations only after that act is recorded. Both cannot hold. Making ADM-02's refusal clause cover any refusal fixes the row that governs it, without adding a case clause.

quotes.text: before it removes the hook registrations, record the widening principal act turning capture off (OWN-11)
Otherwise it MUST list every artifact any ParleyInn component created
offer to remove each, reverse exactly the harness configuration changes `install` made
Until presence proofs ship (OWN-11, OWN-12), ParleyInn MUST refuse every widening act while managed policy requires an authenticator

edits.new: when ParleyInn refuses that act, `parinn uninstall` MUST change nothing, name the reason (under OWN-22, the open residual risks and the runs that leave them open), audit the refusal

themes.title: No scenario step covers losing a device key or device-seat key while the identity stays unchanged
themes.reason: The gap is real and ships in M1 (SEC-10, SEC-27 in part, REC-24). SEC-10's 'missing … minted anew' and REC-24's 'MUST NOT' count as a changed identity, yet neither has a step in any scenario. The REC-24 examples cover only changed identities. The only key-loss step in SEC-27 is a run-seat key lost on a harness resume. This is a coverage gap, not a contradiction or an invariant break in the text, so it is not blocking.

quotes.text: A device key or seat key missing from where it is kept MUST be audited and counted and minted anew, a seat key under SEC-27.
but a device key or seat key missing from where SEC-10 keeps it MUST NOT
a seat key minted on a backup restore, or because a node identity change put the home on another machine, starts a new seat and writer

themes.gap: M1's scenarios must gain a step, with the node identity unchanged, in which a device key and a device seat's key deleted from where SEC-10 keeps them are each audited, counted and minted anew. The new seat key starts a new seat and writer that names the old one, and earlier events stay recorded on this node (SEC-10, SEC-27, REC-24).

themes.title: A rule level tightened through configuration versus OWN-10's principal act
themes.reason: Rule levels take effect only with OWN-04 and OWN-10. Both are P1 OWN rows that §12.2 puts in M7 ('OWN P1 rows but OWN-01'). In M1–M5 no rule level governs any behaviour, so the tension appears only in M7.

quotes.text: Every rule level change the principal makes MUST be a principal act.
until then each setting it changes MUST stand as it stood, while any other change that only tightens, such as turning a B1–B3 component off, needs no acceptance

themes.title: Pins from device seats whose device key was lost before PRV-10 stop qualifying once PRV-10 ships
themes.reason: Until PRV-10 ships, PIN-10 qualifies pins from this node's own device seat whichever device key certified it, so nothing changes in M1–M5. The loss of qualification happens only at the switch to PRV-10's certificate chains, in M7.

quotes.text: A seat certificate a device key made before a principal key certified that key MUST stay valid once one does (PRV-10).

themes.title: No requirement says an assignment refuses no seat's act
themes.reason: Assignments are set only under LANE-09, a P2 row in M8. The capability to set them belongs to the rest of LANE-16 (M7). No M1–M5 behaviour creates an assignment.
